analysis.evidence: In בְּנֵי יֶפֶת, the construct noun בְּנֵי means ‘sons of’ and יֶפֶת names their father. The list of his sons begins with גֹּמֶר.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: גֹּמֶר is the first name after בְּנֵי יֶפֶת (‘sons of Japheth’). The following וּמָגוֹג (‘and Magog’) continues the list, confirming that גֹּמֶר is a personal name here.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add a Hebrew personal-name article for מָגוֹג. The genealogy supports the gloss “Magog” and gives no basis for “dainties” or the proposed root גוב.
draft.definition: Magog is the personal name of one of Japheth’s sons.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:2 identifies Magog by his place in the genealogy. The verse gives no etymology for his name.

analysis.evidence: בְּנֵי יֶפֶת means “the sons of Japheth” and introduces the list in Genesis 10:2. Magog is the second name in that list, between Gomer and Madai.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וּ means “and” and joins the personal name מָגוֹג to the preceding name גֹּמֶר.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for מָדַי. The verse gives no derivation for the name.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:2 lists Madai as the third name under בְּנֵי יֶפֶת, “the sons of Japheth.”

analysis.evidence: The heading בְּנֵי יֶפֶת, “the sons of Japheth,” introduces the list. וּמָדַי names Madai between Magog and Javan.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וּ־, “and,” appears before the initial מ of the personal name מָדַי.

analysis.evidence: The heading בְּנֵי יֶפֶת identifies the names that follow as sons of Japheth. וְיָוָן appears between Madai and Tubal in that list.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וְ means “and” and introduces the proper name יָוָן.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for Tubal. His name’s derivation is uncertain.
draft.definition: Tubal, one of the sons of Japheth.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:2 names Tubal under the heading “the sons of Japheth.”

analysis.evidence: The heading בְּנֵי יֶפֶת, “the sons of Japheth,” identifies the relationship. Tubal appears between Javan and Meshech in that list.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ, “and,” introduces the masculine personal name תּוּבַל, spelled תֻבָל here.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for Meshech. The mashakh article records the identically pointed common noun מֶשֶׁךְ.
draft.definition: Meshech is the personal name of a son of Japheth.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:2 identifies Meshech by his place in the list of Japheth’s sons. The derivation of his name is unknown.

analysis.evidence: בְּנֵי יֶפֶת, “the sons of Japheth,” introduces the list. וּמֶשֶׁךְ names one of those sons between Tubal and Tiras.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וּ means “and” and joins the personal name מֶשֶׁךְ to the preceding name in the list.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for תִּירָס. The verse supports the gloss “Tiras” and gives no basis for “treachery” or the root תחת.
draft.definition: Tiras, the last son named in the list of Japheth’s sons in Genesis 10:2.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:2 ends with וּמֶשֶׁךְ וְתִירָס, “and Meshech and Tiras,” under the heading “the sons of Japheth.”

analysis.evidence: The heading בְּנֵי יֶפֶת means “the sons of Japheth.” The final וְ joins Tiras to the list immediately after Meshech. The verse identifies the bearer but gives no etymology for his name.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ means “and” and introduces the proper noun תִירָס, whose dictionary form is תִּירָס.
